_comment: Ratchet for check_prompt_size.py. These counts only go DOWN. ceiling_chars is enforced only once uncapped_blocks reaches 0, because a sum over an incomplete registry is not a sum: an uncapped block contributes 0, so the ceiling would read as passing while the thing it bounds is unbounded. Driving uncapped_blocks to 0 is the work; re-pinning the other two is not.
because:
First pin, 2026-09-04, from a committed tree. uncapped_blocks pins at 9, NOT the 1 the design predicted: the registry's first act was to find eight more blocks with no byte budget, none of which was reachable by reading any single file. Two of the nine are deliberate rather than debt - ambient_digest caps on ITEMS not bytes (a count is not a byte budget), and custom_instructions is the operator's own L3 text, which must never be capped to fit platform text. ceiling_chars stays UNENFORCED until this count reaches 0, because an uncapped block contributes 0 to the sum and a ceiling over an incomplete sum reads as passing while the thing it bounds is unbounded.

BASELINE HISTORY, 2026-09-17: static_chars re-pinned 23840 -> 24256. Measured cause, not an assertion: the pin was 23840 at 41c8b23c and still 23840 at ef1bffa0~1, and became 24479 at ef1bffa0. That one commit added the DELEGATION_RULE clause 'FILING A TICKET IS NOT DOING THE WORK', and it is the whole of the overrun -- nothing else contributed and no other commit is implicated. The clause was not re-pinned then, which is the defect being closed here.

WHY IT IS KEPT RATHER THAN CUT. It closes a reported behaviour: a chat filed a ticket, handed the work back, and believed it had delivered, because no prompt layer said otherwise. It is also the rule that keeps a chat doing the work in the conversation instead of turning every request into a queue entry the operator then has to go and find. The text has been tightened from 639 chars to 416 (24479 -> 24256), which is as far as it goes without losing the three cases it enumerates; reaching 23840 means deleting the rule.

THIS IS A LOOSENING and is recorded rather than done quietly. check_ratchets_not_loosened.py will flag it, correctly. The way to undo it is to delete the clause from DELEGATION_RULE and re-pin down, or to find 416 chars of genuinely redundant platform prompt text elsewhere, which is the better answer and is not attempted here because trimming prompt text in a hurry is how meaning gets lost.

BASELINE HISTORY, 2026-09-17 (later the same day): static_chars re-pinned DOWN 24256 -> 23922, from the committed tree at 01eae38a. This is the answer the entry above asked for and did not attempt -- "find 416 chars of genuinely redundant platform prompt text elsewhere, which is the better answer" -- and it found 334 of them, in redundancy rather than in trimming. The b8d8abb2 clause that caused the upward pin is NOT deleted: its sentence survives verbatim in DELEGATION_RULE. What went was the three-case enumeration around it plus the TRIAGE sentence that opened TASK_PROPOSAL_BUILD_RULE (-302), because those two and the `auto` mode arm were three answers to one question inside a single assembled prompt, and the most specific of them was making agents do large multi-file work inline. Replacing all three with one ordered rule is what paid for the re-pin. DELEGATION_RULE 2859 -> 2827, TASK_PROPOSAL_BUILD_RULE 2372 -> 2070. Not a loosening, so check_ratchets_not_loosened has nothing to say about it; 23840, the pin before the overrun, is now 82 chars away.
